thread:
Maria G: Quick heads-up — after rolling kernel-selector v2 to canary yesterday, p99 jumped ~120ms on two GPU pools. Replays show a tail shift but synthetic load didn't. Anyone seen this?

benchbot: deploy v2 rolled to us-east-1/gpu-pool-2 @ 11:12 UTC — no crash, health ok. :white_check_mark:

Ajay R: Saw it on canary as well. p50 stable, p99 up. My first suspicion is microbatch auto-sizing interacting with the new kernel pricing out small batch kernels.

Sam L: Could also be KV-cache thrash. Kernel change switched short-seq path to grouped GEMM; that can increase mem pressure and evictions for some traces.

Jen P: Can you paste a minimal reproducer or perf counters? Flamegraph would help.

Maria G: Pasting quick snippet from the replay run and a few lines from the tail trace: 
```
# replay command we ran
./loadgen --trace=prod_replay_2026-03-15.trace --kernel-selector=policy-v2 --autoscale-microbatch=on 
# tail sample (request ids truncated)
2026-03-15T11:18:23Z req=... p99=420ms kernel=grouped-gemm-v2 microbatch=6 kv_hits=0 kv_misses=1
2026-03-15T11:18:24Z req=... p99=450ms kernel=grouped-gemm-v2 microbatch=8 kv_hits=2 kv_misses=4
```

Ajay R: Thanks. I compared a replay run with old kernel vs new kernel: replay p99 old=250ms new=370ms. But when I run synthetic steady-state traffic (constant qps, no think time), p99 is ~260ms both kernels. So it's an interaction with realistic inter-arrival distribution.

Kyle T: Important note: our synthetic harness flattens user think times, which means microbatching patterns differ. That can mask head-of-line waiting and change which kernel gets chosen. We need mixed-fidelity synthetic that injects think-time distribution.

Sam L: Also agree we should run with KV disabled to isolate. Add `--kv-cache=off` to the replay and compare. If tail disappears, it's cache tuning.

Jen P: Also capture batch-width histogram and KV hit/miss histograms for the runs. Quick command to run with more telemetry: 
```bash
./loadgen \
  --trace=prod_replay_2026-03-15.trace \
  --kernel=grouped-gemm-v2 \
  --kv-cache=on \
  --emit-histograms=batch_width,kv_hits \
  --think-factor=0.25
```

Maria G: Good call. We should also diff flamegraphs for CPU/GPU kernels to see where latency is spent — kernel launch vs waiting in microbatch queue.

benchbot: benchmark job created: bench/2065432100-kernel-diff (linked to IC-4723)

Ajay R: I'll run kernel A vs kernel B replay comparisons and kv-off tests today, and upload histograms to the bench job.

Kyle T: I'll modify the harness to replay with injected think-time samples derived from production 95th-percentile inter-arrival distribution, and add a toggle to switch between strict synthetic and mixed-fidelity.

Sam L: I'll pull KV hit-rate timelines and tail traces; will include flamegraphs for the high-p99 window.

Maria G: Plan summary: 1) isolate kernel delta using identical replay trace 2) replay with kv on/off 3) run mixed-fidelity synthetic (think-time injected) vs classic synthetic 4) collect batch-width + kv histograms + flamegraphs 5) compare p95/p99 and tail traces.

Jen P: Suggest adding a microbatch sizing ablation: force microbatch sizes {1,2,4,8} to see knee point vs throughput. That will show whether autoscaler is picking bad widths.

Maria G: Good. Volunteers noted. Assign IC-4723 to the group, please add commits and model names in the bench job. Reconvene tomorrow 10:30 PT in #eng-runtime. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Reminder: include commit hash, model name, and seed in every bench job metadata.

Maria G: Thanks everyone — let's aim to get a deterministic repro before rolling more kernel selector changes.
